analysis:
Compared all supplied base/head route-test source and examined the metadata and bounded patch for scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py. scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py:42-75 now classifies seven macOS CI jobs as routed, replacing their literal-runner requirement; lines 139-146 and 505-526 check independent per-shard lane keys and conditional counts. Existing tests still require exact runner-label arrays, TLS verification, fork fallback, bounded plane failures, sanitized summaries, read-only job permissions and literal release/credentialed runners (head:301-451, 532-548, 567-585). The second script's visible patch similarly replaces literal-runner assertions with route-output assertions. No concrete security regression is established by these test changes alone; they do not alter provider encryption, authorization, attestation or prefix-cache controls, including T-041.
Integration must inspect .github/workflows/ci.yml and darkbloom-route.yml to validate the newly routed jobs' actual permissions, inputs, artifact/cache outputs and failure behavior. Establish the macOS sandbox isolation and runner lifecycle contract rather than treating per-shard lane names or exact labels as proof of isolation. In particular, verify whether test results or caches from these runners influence signed-build qualification or release inputs (A-017, T-054, TB-011), and whether execution can access owner credentials or live provider data (A-019, A-008, A-001). These are unverified cross-file contracts, not findings. The second script has only a truncated patch, so its remaining changes are a coverage limit requiring reconciliation in integration.
